question: The United Nations organisation was set up through the signing of the United Nations Charter by ______ states.
solution:
The correct answer is __**51**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The United Nations Charter was signed on 26 June 1945 in San Francisco at the conclusion of the United Nations Conference on International Organization.
 
• The UN Charter came into force on 24 October 1945, when the United Nations officially came into existence.
 
• Initially, 51 countries signed the United Nations Charter, making them the founding members of the UN.
 
• The purpose of the United Nations, as outlined in its Charter, is to maintain international peace and security, develop friendly relations among nations, achieve international cooperation, and be a center for harmonizing the actions of nations.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **United Nations Charter**

 
 
• The United Nations Charter is the foundational treaty of the United Nations, an intergovernmental organization.
 
• It establishes the structure and purpose of the UN, including the General Assembly, the Security Council, the Economic and Social Council, the International Court of Justice, and the Secretariat.
 
• The Charter outlines the principles of international relations in the aftermath of World War II, emphasizing the importance of peace, human rights, and social progress.
 
• It was signed by 50 original member countries at the United Nations Conference on International Organization in San Francisco, and Poland signed it later, bringing the total number of founding members to 51.
 
 
 
• **United Nations (UN)**
 
 
• The United Nations is an international organization founded in 1945 after World War II by 51 countries committed to maintaining international peace and security, developing friendly relations among nations, and promoting social progress, better living standards, and human rights.
 
• The UN now has 193 member states, and its work is guided by the principles and purposes contained in its founding Charter.
 
• The UN's main bodies include the General Assembly, the Security Council, the Economic and Social Council, the International Court of Justice, and the UN Secretariat.
 
• The UN system also encompasses specialized agencies, programs, and funds such as WHO, UNICEF, and UNESCO, which work on various global issues including health, education, and cultural heritage.
 
 
 
• **San Francisco Conference**
 
 
• The United Nations Conference on International Organization, commonly known as the San Francisco Conference, was held from 25 April to 26 June 1945 in San Francisco, United States.
 
• The conference was attended by representatives of 50 countries, who were involved in drafting and signing the United Nations Charter.
 
• The conference aimed to create an international organization that would replace the League of Nations and prevent another global conflict.
 
• It resulted in the creation of the United Nations and the adoption of its Charter, which laid the groundwork for the post-war international order.
